title: Health at Home — Chronic Disease Management
description: Designed a remote chronic disease management service across UK, Spain, and Brazil, grounded in ethnographic research with patients and nurses. Achieved a 48% reduction in mortality and 63% reduction in hospital readmissions.

sections.title: Context
sections.body: Telefonica Digital / O2, across three markets: O2 UK, Movistar Spain, Vivo Brazil. UX team of up to 17 people across 5 locations.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: Patients with chronic conditions required regular monitoring but hospital visits for routine check-ins were costly and, for many patients, neither feasible nor necessary. Hospital readmission rates were high and preventable. For Telefonica, the business case was proving that health services built on telecoms infrastructure could achieve measurable clinical outcomes — justifying continued investment and commercial rollout.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I led the UX team across the full project: ethnographic research programme, co-creation workshops with clinical staff, and design and delivery of both the patient-facing mobile interface and the clinical dashboard. Team management and delivery oversight were mine. Fieldwork in 5 locations, up to 17 people reporting into my function.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: The project started with ethnographic home visits across multiple patient groups. The critical insight was that patients didn't talk about the technology — they talked about their nurse. The weekly nurse call was the emotional anchor of the service. This shaped the design completely: instead of designing for automation and minimal human contact, I designed a system that optimised nurse time so they could focus on the conversations that mattered. The clinical dashboard was co-designed with nurses, cardiologists, and heads of department. Nurses owned day-to-day monitoring; doctors were involved only when escalated.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body:
• 48% decrease in mortality rate among enrolled patients
  • 63% decrease in hospital readmission rate
  • The patient journey map produced from ethnographic research became a cross-functional reference tool used by product, clinical, and operational teams across all four markets
